Diagnosis: the failure is a pre-Runtime validation mismatch on Windows. In `windows-discovery`, discovery stays non-executing and portable: it uses `exec.LookPath`, then absolute-path candidate scanning, and only checks `filepath.IsAbs(...) && executableAvailable(...)` before recording a runtime. The Windows-specific candidate builder only appends `.exe` under `platform == "windows"`, while the NVM scan explicitly avoids shells/profiles. In `windows-availability`, `executableAvailable` is just `os.Stat` plus regular-file and Unix execute-bit gating, with no Windows branch in the excerpt. In `windows-enrollment`, CLI enrollment independently rejects any resolved Codex path that lacks execute bits. In `windows-console-preflight`, Console sets `ExecutableReady` from the same `executableAvailable(executablePath)` before any Runtime probe. That combination explains why installed native launchers and `codex.cmd` shims can be marked missing/rejected before Runtime is consulted.

Minimal consistent policy: keep discovery unchanged and non-executing, but make launchability validation platform-aware. Preserve the current Unix rule (`regular file + execute bit`). On Windows, accept launchers that the OS can run, including native `.exe` and script launchers such as `.cmd`/`.bat`, without requiring Unix permission bits. Do not change Runtime permissions.
